title: Support MERMAID_RELEASE_VERSION in docs.
body:
## :bookmark_tabs: Summary

When adding a new feature, we can use `(v<MERMAID_RELEASE_VERSION>+)` in the title or description. 
It will be replaced automatically with the current version number when the release happens.

eg: `# Feature Name (v<MERMAID_RELEASE_VERSION>+)`

Unlike normal transformations happening in docs, this will be applied to the source docs file and persisted. 

## :straight_ruler: Design Decisions

As we don't have version specific documentation, (we should have these somehow), a user might be using an older version of mermaid (in a website, plugin, etc) and will get errors when trying out newer features. 

Now the documentation for the features will have the supported version, which can help the user figure out if the feature will work for them or not. 

### :clipboard: Tasks

Make sure you

- [ ] :book: have read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/mermaid-js/mermaid/blob/develop/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [ ] :computer: have added unit/e2e tests (if appropriate)
- [ ] :notebook: have added documentation (if appropriate)
- [ ] :bookmark: targeted `develop` branch
author: sidharthv96

comments.author: aloisklink
comments.body:
I have a couple of issues with this block:

This code currently won't work without giving the `permission: contents: write`, and I'm very uncomfortable with giving this permission to any GitHub Action, since then it would be very easy for malicious code to commit malicious things to the Mermaid repo.

I would much rather prefer if we instead making a **RELEASE.md** file, and in it, we just ask the releaser to manually run these scripts before making the release commit.

If we do still decide to use a GitHub Action to automatically do this, then:

- If we do use `EndBug/add-and-commit`, instead of using `@v9`, we should probably use a Git hash like `@1bad3abcf0d6ec49a5857d124b0bfb52dc7bb081` instead, since that way, we'll only run a new version of this action when [@renovate[bot]](https://github.com/marketplace/renovate) makes a PR.
  - Or maybe we just use some `git commit` commands instead.
- I'd prefer if the author (or at least the commiter) was `41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com`, so that we know that this was an auto-generated commit.

comments.author: sidharthv96
comments.body:
Ok, how about a different approach?

We add a check in `release/*` branch to ensure there is no `MERMAID_RELEASE_VERSION` string present. 
So all release PRs will fail till someone runs the script manually.

comments.author: aloisklink
comments.body:
:+1: That's a great work around!

Maybe the check should also run in the `master` branch too.

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: Raises security concerns about permissions and suggests concrete alternatives: using a RELEASE.md file with manual steps, pinning actions to a Git hash, and setting a specific bot author/committer identity for auto-generated commits.

comments.author: aloisklink

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: Suggests moving the file to the `scripts/` folder and possibly relocating another file as well — implies a structural/organizational change to the codebase.

comments.body:

comments.author: nirname
comments.body: Are we limiting building docs only to master and release? Does not this mean we do not check if the docs are successfully built for PR-s anymore?

comments.author: sidharthv96
comments.body: `pull_request:` is present in the line below. This is specifically for pushes.

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: Flags a potential regression where docs are no longer built/checked for PRs, implying the workflow change should be reconsidered or fixed to restore PR-level doc build checks.

comments.author: nirname
comments.body: Why do we change docs manually? Have we refused from CI that builds docs for us?

comments.author: sidharthv96
comments.body:
This is for the contributors who add features. 

The replacement of MERMAID_RELEASE_VERSION will happen when the release manager runs `pnpm docs:release-version`. 

We removed the CI pushing changes in favour of a manual step.

comments.author: nirname
comments.body: I would not remove the CI because it has some consistency, whereas local development setup does not, even `.lock` do not guarantee that. If someone compiles document it can be a little different every time. But I don't like a robot pushing to my branch either, because this is not obvious.

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: Questions why docs are being changed manually instead of via CI, implying the manual changes may be unnecessary or that the CI-based approach should be restored.
